name: room
text: Room opened — goal: security: Paranoid guard: scan for leaks/injection; VERIFY elements are REAL (not fake/dead); DETECT

name: Warden
text: Deploy LLM Guard as the input/output scanner for all LLM interactions. It’s open-source, actively maintained, and designed specifically to catch prompt injections and data leaks—no need to build a custom solution. The trade-off is accepting its default rule set, which may flag some benign inputs as malicious, but that’s better than missing real threats.

name: Audit
text: Warden’s plan ignores the false-positive risk in LLM Guard’s default rules—those benign inputs it flags could cripple legitimate workflows if the guard blocks critical prompts. A better alternative is to run LLM Guard in audit mode first, tune its rules against real traffic, then deploy only after the false-positive rate drops below 1%. Settle it by measuring the tuned guard’s performance on a 24-hour sample of actual LLM interactions before full rollout.
